subtopics.title: Tilted Strata, Dip Slopes and Scarp Slopes

questions.question: The DIP of a tilted rock layer is:
options: The angle between the layer and the horizontal
The depth of the layer underground
The length of the ridge it forms

questions.question: The dip slope of a tilted ridge:
options: Cuts across the ends of many layers
FOLLOWS the tilted upper surface of one resistant layer, so its angle matches the dip of the rock
Faces the same way as the scarp slope

questions.question: The scarp slope is steep and often cliffed because it:
options: Runs along a single soft layer
CUTS ACROSS the broken edges of layer after layer, truncating the resistant band near the top

questions.question: Strata become tilted through:
options: Crustal movements — compression and folding, unequal uplift, or the sagging and arching of basins

questions.question: A cuesta forms where the strata dip:
options: Gently, up to about 25 degrees — giving a long gentle dip slope and a short steep scarp slope

questions.question: The Magaliesberg near Pretoria is South Africa's textbook example of a:
options: HOMOCLINAL RIDGE — a resistant quartzite ridge with strata dipping steeply between about 25 and 45 degrees

questions.question: A hogsback is near-symmetrical because:
options: With the layers standing beyond about 45 degrees, BOTH sides cut across strata at similar steep angles — the gentle dip-slope ramp disappears

questions.question: As dip increases from gentle to near-vertical, the ridge:
options: Becomes narrower and its two slopes become more EQUAL, until the asymmetry vanishes

questions.question: In a cuesta basin, the slopes of the concentric ridges are arranged with:
options: Dip slopes facing INWARD toward the centre and scarp slopes facing OUTWARD
Dip slopes facing outward and scarps inward

questions.question: Artesian water occurs in cuesta basins because:
options: Water entering a tilted aquifer at the rim flows down the dip and collects under PRESSURE beneath the centre, so boreholes there may flow unaided
The centre of a basin is always a lake

questions.question: In a cuesta dome, the scarp slopes face:
options: INWARD toward each other across the eroded core, because each layer dips down away from the centre

questions.question: South Africa's world-famous ring structure of upturned strata etched into concentric ridges is:
options: The VREDEFORT DOME south-west of Johannesburg, a World Heritage Site

subtopics.title: Reading Tilted Country on the Map

questions.question: On a contour map, a cuesta or homoclinal ridge shows:
options: Contours tightly crowded on ONE side of the crest and widely spaced on the other

questions.question: Crest at 1 500 m; the 1 300 m contour lies 400 m away on the north side and 2 000 m away on the south. The gradients are:
options: North 1 in 2 and south 1 in 10 — so the north is the scarp and the strata dip south

questions.question: With a vertical scale of 1 cm to 100 m and a horizontal scale of 1:50 000, the vertical exaggeration is:
options: 5 times — vertical scale 1:10 000, and 50 000 divided by 10 000 is 5

questions.question: Human activity in tilted-strata country typically places:
options: Highways straight up the scarp faces
Farms on the gentle dip slopes, roads and towns in the strike valleys, and crossings where rivers have cut poorts through the crest — like the Hartbeespoort gap in the Magaliesberg

questions.question: In the tilted lever-arch file picture, the top cover you run your hand down stands for:
options: The DIP SLOPE — the gentle ramp riding on the surface of one strong layer

questions.question: The high END of the file, showing the cut-off edges of all the pages, stands for:
options: The SCARP SLOPE — the steep face slicing across the ends of the layers

questions.question: The memory line 'dip follows, scarp cuts' means:
options: The dip slope is always steeper
Both slopes follow the same layer
The dip slope runs along ONE layer's surface while the scarp slope cuts across MANY layers' edges

subtopics.title: Turning the Dial from Ramp to Hedgehog

questions.question: The three dial settings, in order of increasing tilt, are:
The 'wheelchair ramp with a cliff at the back' describes:
options: A CUESTA — gentle dip slope, short steep scarp, dip up to about 25 degrees

questions.question: At the hedgehog setting, past about 45 degrees, the ramp disappears because:
options: The ridge sinks below the plain
With layers standing nearly upright, both sides cut across page-edges and both are steep — no side follows a layer surface gently anymore

questions.question: The one-sentence trend for the essay is:
options: The steeper the dip, the wider and flatter the ridge
Dip has no effect on ridge shape
The steeper the dip, the narrower the ridge and the more equal its two slopes, until the difference vanishes near vertical

subtopics.title: Soup Bowls, Blisters and Where the Roads Go

questions.question: The nested soup bowls stand for a cuesta basin, in which:
options: Gentle dip slopes face INWARD to the centre and scarp rims face OUTWARD

questions.question: Drilling a borehole near the CENTRE of a cuesta basin can yield:
options: ARTESIAN water that rises on its own, because water entering the tilted layer at the rim collects under pressure below the middle

questions.question: The upside-down blister pile stands for:
options: A CUESTA DOME — dip slopes facing outward, scarps facing inward across the eroded core, like the Vredefort Dome

questions.question: The highway, railway and dam all squeeze through the same gap in the Magaliesberg because:
options: The crest is the flattest ground
The valleys are too wide for roads
Traffic can cross the resistant ridge only where a river has already sawn a poort through it — human routes obey the rock
